bug_description.original: Heap-buffer-overflow in coap_pdu_parse_header OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=512517700 Crash type: Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 Crash state: coap_pdu_parse_header coap_pdu_parse2 coap_pdu_parse
bug_description.normalized: The staged 149-byte `persist_fuzzer` testcase is split into observe, observe-count, and dynamic-resource files. The dynamic-resource segment is accepted as one persisted record with `e_proto == COAP_PROTO_WSS`, a 29-byte name field, and a two-byte saved packet `ed 00`. `coap_op_dyn_resource_load_disk()` recreates a request PDU with `coap_pdu_init(..., 0)`, so vulnerable `coap_pdu_init()` allocates only the header area and leaves `pdu->token` exactly at the end of that heap buffer. `coap_pdu_parse2()` still accepts the two-byte WSS packet because its computed header size is 2, copies `ed 00` into the PDU header buffer, and leaves `used_size == 0`. In `coap_pdu_parse_header()`, the copied header byte `0xed` yields extended token-length marker `0x0d`, so the parser reads `pdu->token[0]` to obtain the extra token-length byte even though no token bytes exist. That single-byte read occurs one byte past the heap allocation and matches the ASan heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 in `coap_pdu_parse_header`.

source.description: First project parser statement that consumes attacker-controlled persisted bytes and materializes the protocol dispatch key for the vulnerable path.
source.value_from: The testcase's third 51-byte segment starts with `06 00 00 00`, so this read sets `*e_proto == 6` (`COAP_PROTO_WSS`), which later selects the two-byte WebSocket header parser that can reach the extended-token logic with only two input bytes.

sink.description: Crash sink. The extended-token branch dereferences the first token byte even though the accepted WSS packet had no bytes after its two-byte header, so `pdu->token[0]` is one byte past the heap buffer allocated by `coap_pdu_init(..., 0)`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. When callers build a parse target with `size == 0`, vulnerable `coap_pdu_init()` allocates only `max_hdr_size` bytes and places `pdu->token` exactly at the end of that allocation. The fix changes this allocation to reserve at least two payload bytes so the later extended-token probes in `coap_pdu_parse_header()` cannot read past the buffer.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific persisted-record admission gate. The testcase's dynamic-resource file contains one structurally accepted record, so the loader does not break here and continues into dynamic resource recreation with attacker-controlled `e_proto`, `name`, and `raw_packet`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This read copies the two saved packet bytes from the testcase into the `raw_packet` buffer that is later parsed.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: After the preceding `ssize_t size` read at line 892 sets `size == 2`, this statement copies the exact packet bytes `ed 00` into `raw_packet->s`.

coarse_trace.summary: The dynamic-resource persistence loader accepts one saved record from the testcase and materializes `e_proto == COAP_PROTO_WSS`, `raw_packet_len == 2`, and `raw_packet == ed 00`.
The loader recreates a request PDU with `coap_pdu_init(..., 0)`, so the parse target has zero payload capacity and its token pointer starts at the end of the allocated header buffer.
WSS parsing treats the two-byte packet as a complete header, copies `ed 00` into the PDU header buffer, and leaves no token bytes because the computed header size equals the packet length.
Header byte `0xed` encodes extended token-length marker `0x0d`, so the parser reads `pdu->token[0]` from beyond the zero-length token area and ASan reports the heap-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.note: The persisted dynamic-resource record begins with little-endian value `6`, so this read materializes `*e_proto == COAP_PROTO_WSS`, the protocol dispatch key for the later parse.
After the 29-byte saved resource name, the next persisted `ssize_t` value is `2`, so the loader materializes a two-byte `raw_packet` length.
Using that length, the loader copies the exact saved packet bytes `ed 00` into `raw_packet->s`.
After one persisted record is admitted, the loader creates the parse target by calling `coap_pdu_init()` with a literal payload size of `0`.

The loader creates the parse target with `size == 0`, so `pdu->alloc_size` stays 0 and the heap allocation is only `pdu->max_hdr_size` bytes. `pdu->token` is therefore positioned exactly one past the last allocated byte.
The reconstructed session inherits `COAP_PROTO_WSS`, so `coap_pdu_parse()` will use the WebSocket header-size logic rather than the four-byte UDP parser.
With `proto == COAP_PROTO_WSS` and packet bytes `ed 00`, header-size parsing returns `2`, so the packet is treated as a complete two-byte WSS header.
Because the saved packet length is exactly the header size, `length - hdr_size == 0`. The parse target keeps zero bytes of token or payload space while header parsing is still allowed to proceed.

fine_trace.code:
if (pdu->token - hdr_size != data)
  memcpy(pdu->token - hdr_size, data, length);
fine_trace.note: The parser copies the accepted packet bytes `ed 00` into the PDU header buffer immediately before `pdu->token`, so later `hdr[0]` reads the copied `0xed` from this local buffer.
Header byte `0xed` has low nibble `0x0d`, so the parser interprets the token-length field as the one-byte extended-token marker `COAP_TOKEN_EXT_1B_TKL`.

The branch for marker `0x0d` unconditionally reads the first token byte to obtain the extra length value. Since steps 5 and 8 left no bytes after the header, this dereference lands one byte past the heap allocation and produces the observed ASan READ 1.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Patch-only evidence: the fix reserves at least two bytes in coap_pdu_init() for extended-token probes, but Stage 02 did not run the fixed build.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: The preserved sanitizer log reports a heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 and the public crash state names `coap_pdu_parse_header -> coap_pdu_parse2 -> coap_pdu_parse`; the full symbolized runtime stack was not preserved.

format.name: libcoap persist_fuzzer dynamic-resource record
format.contract: The third testcase segment (51 bytes) must decode as one persisted dynamic-resource record with little-endian `e_proto == 6` (`COAP_PROTO_WSS`), a 29-byte saved resource name, little-endian `raw_packet_len == 2`, and exact saved packet bytes `ed 00`. Those two packet bytes make WSS header parsing accept a two-byte header whose first byte carries extended token-length marker `0x0d` but leaves no token byte to read.
